value.title: Shared synthesize() reducer, arch-lens catalog, and architect.panel config
value.description: Build the reusable foundation with zero behavior change: a pure synthesize() ranking/synthesis reducer (alongside the untouched reconcile()), an arch-lens prompt catalog (src/orchestrator/arch-lenses.ts), and the opt-in architect.panel config in the Zod schema. Pure functions + config only; no orchestrator wiring yet.

successCriteria.description: src/orchestrator/workflow/synthesizer.ts exports `synthesize(approaches, lensScores, ...)` returning a SynthesisResult { winner, ranking: Array<{ approach, perLensScores, total }> (ordered desc by total), graftedIdeas: string[], dissent: string[] }. It is PURE (no Date.now/new Date/Math.random/fs — any timestamp is a caller arg). Tie-break is deterministic and documented (e.g. earliest approach index wins on equal total). Unit tests cover: clear winner, a tie resolved deterministically, and dissent capture (a lens whose top pick differs from the winner is recorded in dissent).

src/orchestrator/arch-lenses.ts exports `resolveArchLensFocus(lens: string): string` over an ARCH_LENS_CATALOG mapping scalability/security/cost/operability/maintainability/reversibility to DISTINCT non-empty focus fragments, returning a generic non-empty fallback for unknown lenses without throwing. A unit test asserts the six built-ins are distinct + non-empty and an unknown lens returns the generic fallback.

architect.panel { enabled: z.boolean().default(false), lenses: z.array(z.string()).default([]), maxConcurrent: z.number().int().min(1).default(4) }.default({...}) is added to the architect config in src/config/schema.ts, mirrored in createDefaultConfig and every other config literal tsc flags (defaults.ts, init.ts, loader.ts, mcp/tools/init.ts). A schema test asserts the defaults and that a config without architect.panel still parses to the default.
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, and npx eslint src/ exit 0; the full vitest suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented pre-existing skipped baseline.

value.title: TS Checkpoint 2 synthesis panel
value.description: Refactor the monolithic runArchitect so Checkpoint 2 (approach selection) becomes a discrete seam: when architect.panel is on, generate candidate approaches, fan out one lens scorer per lens (bounded by maxConcurrent), synthesize() a ranked winner, and select it. When the panel is off, runArchitect runs the existing single monolithic agentic loop byte-identically.

successCriteria.description: When architect.panel is unset/disabled OR lenses.length<2, runArchitect runs the existing single monolithic runAgenticLoop and returns an ArchitectResult equivalent to today. A unit test mocks createClient/runAgenticLoop and asserts the off path takes the single-loop branch (one runAgenticLoop call, no lens fan-out).

When architect.panel.enabled with >=2 lenses, CP2 generates candidate approaches then issues one judge call per lens scoring those approaches through resolveArchLensFocus(lens), never exceeding maxConcurrent concurrent calls, and synthesize() produces the ranked winner which becomes the selected approach. A mocked-client test asserts call-count == lenses.length, peak concurrency <= maxConcurrent, and that the selected approach equals synthesize().winner.

The selected approach and per-lens scores flow into the architecture document / ADR-1, and CP1/CP3/CP4/CP5 still run to produce the full ArchitectResult. The ArchitectResult shape is unchanged except an additive optional lensScores field; a result without it still validates.
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npx eslint src/ exit 0; the full vitest suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented pre-existing skipped baseline.

nonGoals: Do NOT add the CP5 review panel — that is sprint 3 (CP5 stays as today this sprint).
Do NOT touch the native surface (skills/agents/commands) — sprints 4-5.
Do NOT modify synthesize()/arch-lenses.ts (built in sprint 1) or reconcile().
Do NOT change CP1/CP3/CP4 behavior, the ArchitectResult shape (beyond additive optional lensScores), or the architecture-doc save path.
Do NOT invoke a real LLM in tests — mock createClient and runAgenticLoop.
stopConditions: Stop when the off path is the unchanged single monolithic loop, the on path generates approaches + fans out lens scorers bounded by maxConcurrent + synthesize()s the winner, and typecheck/build/lint/tests are green.
Stop when changes are confined to src/orchestrator/architect-agent.ts and its test (plus the additive optional lensScores on the ArchitectResult interface).

value.title: TS Checkpoint 5 review panel
value.description: Refactor runArchitect Checkpoint 5 (review/assembly) into a discrete seam: when architect.panel is on, assemble the draft architecture + ADRs, fan out one lens reviewer per lens (bounded by maxConcurrent), and reconcile() a pass/fail verdict (fail-closed on tie) that gates final assembly. When off, CP5 runs as today (single-agent within the monolithic loop), byte-identical.

successCriteria.description: When architect.panel is disabled OR lenses.length<2, CP5 runs as today (the existing single-agent review within the monolithic flow); the off path is byte-identical (mocked-client test asserts no per-lens review fan-out on the off path).

When the panel is on, CP5 issues one review call per lens through resolveArchLensFocus(lens), bounded by maxConcurrent, each returning a pass/fail verdict, and reconcile() yields the panel verdict. A unit test asserts call-count == lenses.length, peak concurrency <= maxConcurrent, and that a 2-pass/2-fail set reconciles to passed=false (fail-closed).

reconcile() is imported from src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.ts and reused unchanged (not reimplemented). The reconciled verdict + per-lens reviews are surfaced on ArchitectResult via an additive optional lensReviews field, and the architecture doc/ADRs still save to .bober/architecture/. A failing panel verdict is recorded in the final assembly (e.g. flagged in the result) rather than silently dropped.
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npx eslint src/ exit 0; the full vitest suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented pre-existing skipped baseline.
